<!-- Generated by docs-site/scripts/generate_reference.py from plugins/airgap-anything/skills/airgap-transfer/references/channels.md. Do not edit. -->
Every channel ends as a folder of files, so the bundle is the same. `transfer.channel` from `blueprint.json` changes only how files are split and in which order they are sent.

| Channel | Rule |
|---|---|
| `removable_media` | The largest file is 4 GiB minus one byte on `fat32` and unlimited on the others. Larger files are split, and so is any file larger than one medium. Files go onto volumes of `medium.capacity_gb`, minus a 2 % reserve, largest first. Every volume carries every file `pack.py` writes (`bundle.json`, `SHA256SUMS`, `PARTS.txt`, `VOLUMES.txt`, the inventory, the inside scripts and the runbook), so that any one volume tells what the set holds and what is missing. |
| `data_diode` | Nothing comes back, so the bundle must be complete and check itself. `channel.max_file_gb` sets splitting; the bundle is one volume. `SEND-ORDER.txt` lists the files in sending order, `bundle.json` and `SHA256SUMS` first, so that the inside can check files as they arrive. A resend uses the same names. Write volume 1 to the folder the diode sends from. |
| `staging_host` | The bundle lands on the staging host, where it is scanned. `channel.max_file_gb` sets splitting; the bundle is one volume. `verify.sh` can run there too, before the move inside. Write volume 1 to the staging host's folder. |
| `other` | As `removable_media` when a medium is named; with `medium.capacity_gb` set to `none`, one volume and no splitting. |

## Scanning stations

On any channel the files may pass a scanning station first:

- `INVENTORY.md` and `INVENTORY.csv` name the kind, source and licence of every file, largest first: scanning hundreds of gigabytes takes time.
- Model weights are safetensors unless the user allowed pickle files for a model; the inventory marks those files.
- Publisher checksum files were checked on the connected side. Signatures are not checked by this version.

## Writing the volumes

`pack.py --write-volume N --to <folder>` copies volume N, cuts the parts of split files on the way, writes `VOLUME.txt` ("volume 2 of 3"), and reads every file back.

| Exit | Meaning | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Every file read back matches | Label the medium with the volume number and write the next one |
| 1 | The medium could not be written, or a file read back differently | The medium may be faulty: write the volume again, or use another medium |
| 2 | No such volume, the folder is not a mounted medium, too little room, or a bundle file changed after `pack.py` | Do what the message says; after a change, run `pack.py` and `check.py` again |

Write one medium at a time.
